clue.text: There's not much time to get food prepared now

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a very short time
a dish is food made ready for the table

explanation.surface: Someone in a hurry has barely a moment to get a meal ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now' looks like part of the surface's urgency but is an adjective meaning fashionable, as in 'the now look'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as 'now' is current and in vogue, a synonym for fashionable.

clue.text: This writer beginning to resent publisher's change? Hard author!

parts.note: the setter referring to themself gives me

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of resent is used

parts.note: an edit is an alteration made to a text before publication
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A writer resents changes forced on them by a publisher and calls the author hard.
explanation.walkthrough: George Meredith was a Victorian English novelist and poet.
explanation.definitionFit: George Meredith, the Victorian novelist, is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Fed up with business community not quite admitting one financial problem?

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the others
in a down clue, up means the word fed is written bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone tired of the business world finds it slow to admit a money problem.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses; 'admitting' takes the numeral in between the two other pieces. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is a shortfall where spending exceeds income, a classic financial problem.

clue.text: The female larked about, being a flighty type

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of larked are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman fooled around, showing herself to be a frivolous sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LARKED into LDRAKE. 'Flighty' looks like a description of character but means able to fly: a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelduck drake is a duck, a bird, so literally a type given to flight.

clue.text: Commander involved in what could be false bit of documentation?

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so one piece sits within the other
what could be signals that the letters of false might form something else

parts.note: taken as written
CIC is short for commander-in-chief

explanation.surface: A senior officer is implicated in what may be a forged document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be' signals the anagram and 'involved in' the container; the commander sits in the middle of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascicle is an instalment of a book published in parts, one section of a larger document.

clue.text: What'ome'asinbathroom that'elps the ventilation?

parts.note: read with dropped aitches, this is what a home has in the bathroom that helps: a hair product with its H dropped too, while the whole names a cooling machine

explanation.surface: A Cockney-style speaker asks what a home keeps in the bathroom to help with airflow.
explanation.walkthrough: Every H is dropped in the clue, a signal to drop the H from the hair product found in bathrooms; what remains names a machine that cools and ventilates rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that cools and circulates indoor air is the ventilation device the dropped-aitch phrase describes.

clue.text: Only a small vehicle needed to take a Liberal group?

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a small car for hire
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: Just a little taxi is needed to carry a Liberal party group.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that the Liberals are so few that one cab can carry them all.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a small secretive faction or clique, a kind of group.

clue.text: It's hot desire that corporal punishment will restrict

indicators.note: restrict means hem in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: the cane, a stick for beating pupils, was a form of corporal punishment
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A provocative remark linking lust and being beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hot' is a definition by description: a hot thing, here a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne pepper is a fiery red spice, so it is something hot.

clue.text: Feature of aeroplane that provides fresh energy for ascent

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascent means the pieces are written going upwards, reversed

parts.note: novel means new or fresh
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An aircraft part that gives a plane extra power for climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: NOVEL then E, read upwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevon is a control surface on a delta wing combining elevator and aileron functions, part of an aircraft.

clue.text: Abandonment of a peculiar match involving drugs

indicators.note: doing something with abandon means wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange football match is called off amid a drugs scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: All fourteen letters of 'a peculiar match' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharmaceutical is the adjective for medicinal drugs and their preparation.

clue.text: New student's touching on activity for older hands boning up?

definitions.text: activity for older hands boning up?

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
a fresher is a first-year university student; the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: A new student discusses something for experienced staff who are swotting up.
explanation.walkthrough: A fresher is British slang for a first-year undergraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course updates the knowledge of experienced people revising their skills.

clue.text: Be angry when this scientist gets a hearing

indicators.note: gets a hearing means the synonym is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: to boil is to seethe with anger

explanation.surface: A furious scientist is finally given the chance to present his case.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Boyle was the seventeenth-century chemist behind Boyle's law.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Boyle, the Anglo-Irish chemist and physicist, is a famous scientist.

clue.text: Winning goal? Side's half cut with drink later

indicators.note: later places the drink after the first piece
half cut means half the word is removed, leaving the back half of side

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A team's match-winner was a bit drunk, then drank some more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' looks like British slang for tipsy, prompting a drinking surface, but it halves SIDE to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal that settles a match is the decisive one, the score that breaks the tie.

clue.text: English poet briefly meeting men in US city

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: briefly means the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Walter Savage Landor was an English poet

explanation.surface: A British poet's short visit to an American city to meet some men.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Savage Landor (1775-1864) was an English poet; dropping his final R gives LANDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a large city in Florida, home of major theme parks.

clue.text: A group of four short fish

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tetrad is a set of four

explanation.surface: Four small fish swim together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like a description of the fish but cuts the last letter off TETRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The tetra is a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater species kept in aquariums.

clue.text: Very devoted theologian, I will have taken a role outside

indicators.note: outside means the acting word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to have acted is to have played a part
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A deeply religious scholar says he will have acted a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' makes the acting word wrap the others, which go in just after its first letter; 'will have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be addicted is to be utterly given over to something, extremely dedicated.

clue.text: Prisoners taken in reportedly getting cramp

parts.note: cons are convicts

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard rather than as written

parts.note: to be taken in is to be tricked or fooled

explanation.surface: Prisoners being received into jail are said to get muscle spasms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cramp' is a verb here, meaning restrict, not the painful spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to hem in or restrict, the same as squeezing tight.

clue.text: In grass the green colour came back

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
vert is the heraldic name for green

explanation.surface: Green returned to the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Vert is green in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to go back to a former state, to return.

clue.text: A bit beyond the yard may be heard some beastly walkers?

indicators.note: may be heard means the phrase is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: a yard is three feet, so a little more is four feet

explanation.surface: Animal footsteps can be heard just past the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A yard is an imperial length of three feet; 'yard' looks like a garden in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The front feet of a four-legged animal are what it walks on, so animal walkers.

clue.text: Firm set up needs leading American to become influential organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Co is short for company
top means leading or foremost
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A company being set up needs a top American to become a powerful body.
explanation.walkthrough: An organisation with far-reaching tentacles is figuratively called by the name of the eight-armed sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a sprawling body with power reaching everywhere is likened to a many-armed sea animal.

clue.text: Imposing awarder of prizes a bit confused at the end

indicators.text: a bit confused at the end
indicators.note: a slight muddle at the end means the last two letters of the prize-giver are switched

parts.note: Alfred Nobel founded the Nobel prizes

explanation.surface: A grand prize-giver gets a little muddled at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final EL of NOBEL is rearranged, giving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble can mean stately or grand in appearance, like an impressive building.

clue.text: What's sold by haberdasher with wrong barcode

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of barcode are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A draper sells an item labelled with the wrong price code.
explanation.walkthrough: A haberdasher is a shop selling fabrics, sewing goods and trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a rich woven fabric with raised patterns, the kind of cloth a draper stocks.

clue.text: Squirm, issuing legal document to ambassador

parts.note: a writ is a written court order
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador wriggles when served with court papers.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and wriggle, as in pain or embarrassment.

clue.text: Rodent caught by the springing mechanical device

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: springing means leaping about, so the letters of the are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rat is caught by a sprung trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'springing' rearranges THE into HET.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed wheel and pawl that allows motion in one direction only, a mechanism.

clue.text: A lot of people worked in the oldest profession from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear means the word is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: prostitution is jokingly called the oldest profession, so to work in it is to have whored

explanation.surface: Many people are rumoured to have worked as prostitutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the oldest profession' is a euphemism for prostitution.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or throng.

clue.text: Event in the open — do 29!

parts.note: out means revealed or no longer hidden
29 across means be there, and to come is to be present

explanation.surface: An outdoor event with an invitation to be there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do 29' tells you to perform the action of 29 across, be present: come.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is a result, something that comes out of events, so a happening.

clue.text: Soak transplant when it falls over

indicators.note: falling over means the word is turned upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to repot a plant is to transplant it to a new pot

explanation.surface: A transplanted plant tips over and gets drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' looks like a verb but is a noun meaning a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A soak is a drunkard, and a toper is a habitual heavy drinker.

clue.text: Nectar? It is about eating prime bit of pork crackling!

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the pork letter goes inside the anagram
about means turned around, so the letters of nectar and it are rearranged
the prime bit is the first letter of the word pork

explanation.surface: A rapturous remark: nectar indeed, pork crackling!
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' gives CREITANT and 'eating' takes P in. 'crackling' looks like the pork snack, but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepitant means making a crackling sound, from Latin crepitare, to crackle.

clue.text: Wind at the back putting any number off in cathedral

indicators.note: in means the shortened word is placed inside the cathedral

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire is a cathedral city

indicators.note: putting with off means removing something from the word
putting off means taking the number away from the word for at the back

parts.note: astern means at the rear of a ship
N is used in mathematics for any number

explanation.surface: A wind blowing from behind as someone stops counting in a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... off' drops the number and 'in' puts the rest just after the cathedral's first letter. Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: Be there to feed up unfeminine daughter

indicators.note: un-feminine means without feminine, so the abbreviation F is taken away

parts.note: to fatten is to feed someone up

explanation.surface: A parent arrives to give a boyish daughter a good meal.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the abbreviation for feminine; 'unfeminine' removes it from FATTEN, leaving ATTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present at an event is the meaning of this verb, as in going to a meeting.
